correctness.rationale: The source's Eq. (14), normalization and factors of 1/2 match the claim, and its Eqs. (3) and (12) specialize to Δ=0 and γ=i cot(πs/2) on the stated branch. At j=0, a0=g u1. At j=1 the forward coefficient vanishes, and eliminating u1 yields (g²−1/2)sin(πs)=0. Conversely at g²=1/2 the computed u1 solves both rows with any u2, so sufficiency is exactly for these two rows. At s=i log(3)/π the displayed relation has γ=coth(log(3)/2)=2 and sin(πs)=i sinh(log 3) is nonzero, so g=1 does give an admissible obstruction. Checked the repaired statement for scope: it does not conclude existence at resonance for the whole sequence, or nonexistence of the physical steady state away from resonance. No numerical or formal verification is required for the calculation.
